sentences.text: Finally, remember how Rule nineteen hands over to the other rules.
The moment two vessels come into sight of one another visually, the rules for vessels in sight, eleven through eighteen, take over, and a stand-on and give-way vessel exist again.
Until then, both vessels share the duty.
Radar contact alone never puts vessels in sight of one another, and Rule seven’s warning about scanty radar information applies with full force in fog.
We’ll cover the fog signals themselves, Rule thirty-five, in lesson fourteen.
